study.title: Exploring the Patterns of Acupuncture on Mild Cognitive Impairment Patients Using Regional Homogeneity
study.study_design: non-repeated event-related (NRER) fMRI design; two-group comparison (MCI patients and age-matched healthy controls); within-subject comparison of pre- and post-acupuncture resting state
study.population: 12 MCI patients and 12 age-matched healthy control subjects
study.disease_condition: mild cognitive impairment (MCI); specifically amnestic MCI
study.inclusion_criteria: MCI patients diagnosed using criteria for amnestic MCI, with Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores between 25 and 27, and Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) scale scores of 0.5. Healthy control subjects recruited from a community. All subjects were right-handed according to the Edinburgh Handedness Inventory. All subjects were acupuncture naive.
study.exclusion_criteria: Subjects were excluded if they had any significant medical, neurological, or psychiatric illness, or if they were taking medication or other substances known to influence cerebral function.

conditions.scan_context: resting state fMRI without any stimulation; subjects kept eyes closed and remained relaxed without engaging in any mental tasks

conditions.scan_context: resting state fMRI without any stimulation following acupuncture; subjects kept eyes closed and remained relaxed without engaging in any mental tasks

extraction_notes.note: The paper reports 'no significant main effect of acupuncture and interactions between group and acupuncture' from the two-way ANCOVA, but subsequently presents post-hoc two-sample t-test and paired t-test results showing group and acupuncture differences. The authors acknowledge that post-hoc tests were exploratory and that the ANCOVA showed no significant effects after multiple corrections.
No sham acupuncture arm was included in this study. The study is a comparison between MCI patients and healthy controls, with no sham or placebo control condition.
Adverse events are not reported in the paper.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not formally assessed or reported beyond stating all subjects were acupuncture naive.
No trial registration number is reported.

Figure 2 shows frequency (%) and intensity (mean ± SE) of deqi sensations for MCI and HC groups across six sensations (soreness, numbness, fullness, warmth, heaviness, tingling). Exact numeric values for all subscales other than warmth (58% MCI, 50% HC) and tingling (16% MCI, 8% HC) are readable only from the figure and not explicitly stated in text. The intensity values are shown with SE bars in Figure 2B but only described as 'approximately similar' in text.

Figure 3 shows KCC maps for HC_REST, MCI_REST, HC_POST_ACU, MCI_POST_ACU. Coordinates or specific cluster information from these maps are not reported in tables; only the threshold (p<0.05 FDR correction) is stated.
Figure 4 shows brain areas with significant main effect of group from ANCOVA at p<0.001 uncorrected. Table 2 provides the corresponding coordinates; extraction relies on Table 2.

The abstract states that in pre-acupuncture resting state MCI patients showed increased ReHo in 'precentral gyrus (PCG), superior frontal gyrus (SFG), and insula (INS)' and decreased in 'middle temporal gyrus (MTG), parahippocampal (PHIP) and cingulate cortex.' Table 3 also includes Cuneus as an increased region, which is not mentioned in the abstract. Extraction follows Table 3 which is more complete.

Table 6 title says 'between healthy controls and MCI patients after acupuncture' but the results describe MCI vs HC (MCI patients showing increased or decreased values). Negative Z-scores in Table 6 indicate decreased ReHo in MCI patients. Positive Z-scores indicate increased ReHo in MCI patients. This interpretation is consistent with Figure 7 caption.
The y-coordinate for the Inferior Temporal Gyrus row in Table 6 appears as '-20' in the OCR'd table. The value '–20' was preserved as -20.
The paper states images were normalized to 'standard MNI template in SPM5' and coordinates are labeled MNI throughout. The coordinate space is taken as MNI based on this explicit statement.

The two-way ANCOVA for global mean ReHo across groups and acupuncture found no changes (P<0.05 threshold stated), but this is distinct from the voxelwise ANCOVA results. The paper uses the same ANCOVA framework for global mean testing and voxelwise testing.

The paper does not report needle retention time separately from the scan duration. The needle was inserted at the start of the acupuncture run (9 minutes total), but exact needle-in time is not given as a standalone numeric field.
Table 6 had some formatting artifacts in the PDF OCR (rows running together). All 13 rows were extracted based on the visible table data and cross-referenced with the results text.
